introduction: “Return” is a word the scriptures use and believers have often taken literally. These readings explain it. When Jesus said that John the Baptist was Elijah, and John said that he was not, both spoke the truth: the person had not come back, the qualities had. So with last year’s rose and this year’s, last night’s lamplight and tonight’s, the seed sown and the seed harvested. The Báb and Bahá’u’lláh apply this to themselves and to their followers and opponents: in every revelation the former one returns, with its faithful and its deniers, and the Manifestations are one reality appearing again under a new name. The Elijah texts are given in full beside the readings, with Paul’s seed, the Qur’án’s “as We began the first creation, We shall repeat it,” Krishna’s “age after age,” and the sayings of Jesus about going away and coming again. The readings deny that souls come back, so Plato and the Gita are quoted for reincarnation. The angels’ promise of “this same Jesus,” the warning against false Christs and the Seal of the Prophets state the three hardest objections.
questions: Jesus said John was Elijah; John said he was not. How does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reconcile them, and does Luke’s phrase “in the spirit and power of Elias” support him?
The readings deny the return of individual souls; Plato and the Gita affirm it. What is at stake in the difference for how a person lives one life?

“In every subsequent Revelation, the return of the former Revelation is a fact,” including its opponents. What does it mean to say that those who rejected Jesus “returned” in those who rejected Muḥammad or the Báb? Could it be said of people today?

Acts promises that “this same Jesus” will come “in like manner”; Jesus warns against anyone who says “Lo, here is Christ.” How would you explain the Bahá’í understanding of return to a Christian who holds both verses?
“I was Noah in the day of Noah.” What is the “I” in that sentence? Compare “before Abraham was, I am.”
Bahá’u’lláh says to Jews and Christians: if you wish to crucify Jesus again, or slay Muḥammad, put me to death. What is he asking each community to recognize about itself?

outside.why: “When Christ said, ‘This is Elias,’ He meant: This person is a manifestation of the … attributes” of Elias. The saying: if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.
The promise behind the saying, in the last verses of the Hebrew prophets: behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord.
Luke’s Gospel gives the interpretation in an angel’s words before John is born: he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias.
“Last year’s rose hath returned to the garden this year.” The Preacher on the returns of nature: the sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.
“This lamplight is last night’s come back again.” Rúmí: the lamps are different, but the Light is the same.
Return is “not the return of the essence but of the attributes.” The Bible had already spoken of Elijah in that way within his own lifetime: the spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha.
“Elijah came but was not recognized in John.” Jesus: Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed.
John himself, asked the question, “said, ‘No, I am not Elias.’” John’s Gospel: art thou Elias? And he saith, I am not.

“Not that he was Elias - the same soul or personality.” Plato held that it is the same soul that comes back: the soul, as being immortal, and having been born again many times, has knowledge of all things. Why do the readings insist that qualities return and persons do not?
“Neither the body nor the soul will return to this world.” The Letter to the Hebrews: it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.

No soul returns. The Bhagavad Gita teaches a soul that changes bodies as a man changes clothes: so putteth by the spirit lightly its garb of flesh, and passeth to inherit a residence afresh. What does each teaching say about why a human life matters?
View “all the Prophets and Messengers of God as one soul and one body.” The Qur’án: we make no distinction between any of His messengers.
“The first among them would be last and the last would be first.” Revelation: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.
“Amongst the many prophets, only Elias was said to return.” The expectation was so alive that people guessed it of Jesus: some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias.
Herod thought a dead prophet had come back in a living one: this is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead.

The seeds of the new harvest are not the seed that was sown, yet its essence has reappeared. Jesus: except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.
Paul uses the seed for the same question of what comes back: that which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain; but God giveth it a body.
Bahá’u’lláh is the Lote Tree, “the teachers and prophets the Branches and the believers, the leaves.” Jesus used the figure of one plant for himself and his own: I am the vine, ye are the branches.
“The Sun of Reality has numerous daysprings.” A psalm: from the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the Lord’s name is to be praised.
One sun and many dawning-places. Malachi: unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings.

“The difference in the manifestations … should not veil the observer, for that which is manifest in all is one Command.” The Letter to the Hebrews: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets.
Krishna: I rise, from age to age, and take visible shape, and move a man with men.
“In every subsequent Revelation, the return of the former Revelation is a fact,” its believers and its opponents included. Stephen saw the opponents return: as your fathers did, so do ye.
Jesus on those who were sure they would have behaved better: ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.
The response returns with the revelation. John’s summary of the first coming would serve for each: he came unto his own, and his own received him not.
The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done.
“The end is like unto the beginning.” God in Isaiah: I am the first, and I am the last.
The Letter to the Hebrews: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
Muḥammad and those around him “have all returned to this world.” The Báb builds on a verse of the Qur’án: as We began the first creation, We shall repeat it.
The promise on which Christian expectation of a return rests. Jesus: I will come again, and receive you unto myself.

Return is the appearance of the same reality in another person. The angels at the ascension promise something more literal: this same Jesus shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven. What would a Christian who waits for “this same Jesus” have to reconsider, and what might he fairly ask in return?

Jesus also left a warning that makes any claim of return hard to hear: if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, believe it not. For there shall arise false Christs. By what tests do the readings expect a true return to be told from a false one?
He “came unto you, yet ye knew Him not.” Two disciples walked seven miles beside the risen Jesus: but their eyes were holden that they should not know him.
“This is indeed ‘Alí Who hath appeared once again.” The oneness that such a sentence assumes was claimed by Jesus across two thousand years: before Abraham was, I am.
“The Friend of God and He Who conversed with God have returned.” On a mountain in Galilee three disciples saw Moses and Elias talking with him.
“He Who conversed with Moses from the Burning Bush hath appeared.” Exodus: God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses.

God is praised by the names each Book gave to the One to come: “the Comforter and Spirit of Truth in the Gospel.” John: he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; even the Spirit of truth.
“If ye be intent on crucifying once again Jesus … put Me to death.” Dostoevsky imagined Christ returning to Seville and the Church’s Inquisitor telling him: why, then, hast Thou come to hinder us?
Those who honour a dead Prophet may be ready to kill a living one. Jesus: your fathers killed them, and ye build their sepulchres.

“In each Revelation the Manifestations gone before were subjected to denial.” The Qur’án: is it ever so, that, when there cometh unto you a messenger with that which ye yourselves desire not, ye grow arrogant, and some ye disbelieve and some ye slay?

The Return expected by the Shí‘ih was that of Ḥusayn. An English historian on why that name holds such power: in a distant age and climate, the tragic scene of the death of Hosein will awaken the sympathy of the coldest reader.
The Báb and Bahá’u’lláh are compared to John the Baptist and Jesus. John: he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear.
The herald yields to the one he announced, as the Báb did. John the Baptist: he must increase, but I must decrease.
Bahá’u’lláh cites the Gospel on going away and the Comforter coming. The passage: it is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you.
“To say what I have not said.” Jesus: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.

“Did We not give you glad tidings of My appearance after Me?” Moses gave such tidings: the Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken.
The goal is “the recognition of God in the Manifestation of His Self, Who hath come yet again.” Old Simeon, who had waited all his life and recognized a child: mine eyes have seen thy salvation.
“I have been before and shall be hereafter.” Wisdom speaks so in Proverbs: when he prepared the heavens, I was there.
Jesus in prayer: glorify thou me with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.
“I was Noah in the day of Noah, and Abraham in the day of Abraham.” Paul of Christ: he is before all things, and by him all things consist.

One reality present in every age under different names. Wordsworth felt something like pre-existence in every child: the Soul that rises with us, our life’s Star, hath had elsewhere its setting, and cometh from afar. How is the Báb’s claim different in kind from the poet’s intuition about all souls?

The first believers were so detached “that even the mention of the Seal … did not prevent them.” The text that stood in their way: he is the messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. If return means the same reality in a new person, in what sense can any Prophet be the last?

The holy ones in Paradise “yearn to return unto this world, and be of some service.” Paul felt the pull both ways: having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better: nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you. What does it say about this world that the blessed should wish to come back to serve in it?

And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to make ready a people prepared for the Lord

john-i-will-come-again.text: In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also

john-glory-before-the-world-was.text: And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was

kings-spirit-of-elijah-doth-rest-on-elis.text: And when the sons of the prophets which were to view at Jericho saw him, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. And they came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him

matthew-john-the-baptist-risen-from-the-.text: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus, And said unto his servants, This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead; and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him
